steps.say: Every head injury assessment starts the same way. You score the eyes, the voice and the movement, and that single number decides scans, referral and intubation.
steps.tx: The **Glasgow Coma Scale** (consciousness score) sums **eye opening** (eye response) **1 to 4** (one to four), **verbal response** (speech reply) **1 to 5** (one to five) and **motor response** (movement reply) **1 to 6** (one to six), giving a total of **3** (deepest coma) to **15** (fully awake) recorded as E, V and M subscores.

vis.alt: Reference chart of Glasgow Coma Scale eye, verbal and motor responses with severity bands.
vis.caption: Glasgow Coma Scale eye, verbal and motor responses with severity bands. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The number sorts patients into three bands. Eight or less means coma and a tube, while thirteen to fifteen can often be watched after a scan.
steps.tx: **Severe injury** (coma band) is a GCS of **8 or less** (eight or less) and needs intubation, **moderate injury** (middle band) is **9 to 12** (nine to twelve) with admission and repeat scanning, and **mild injury** (minor band) is **13 to 15** (thirteen to fifteen) with discharge only after a normal scan and a responsible adult at home.

rows: Record E plus V plus M

steps.say: NICE tells you exactly who needs a scan within the hour. Learn this list cold, because examiners love testing the exceptions.
steps.tx: NICE orders CT within **1 hour** (one hour) for GCS below **13** (thirteen) on arrival, GCS below **15** (fifteen) at **2 hours** (two hours), suspected open or depressed or **basal skull fracture** (base of skull break), **post-traumatic seizure** (fit after injury), focal deficit, or **more than one vomit** (repeated vomiting).

steps.say: Blood thinners change the rules completely. A normal examination never excludes a bleed when the patient is anticoagulated.
steps.tx: Anticoagulated patients with any **loss of consciousness** (blackout) or amnesia need CT within **8 hours** (eight hours) even when fully alert, because **warfarin** (vitamin K blocker) and **direct oral anticoagulants** (newer thinners) let small veins bleed slowly into large clots.

steps.say: Radiologists grade the scan with Marshall. The grade predicts death, so a grade three scan earns an ICU bed even when the patient looks well.
steps.tx: The **Marshall classification** (CT injury grade) runs diffuse injury **I to IV** (one to four) by cistern compression and shift, with **V** (five) for an evacuated mass and **VI** (six) for a non-evacuated mass, and mortality climbs with each grade from roughly one in ten to more than half.

steps.say: Rotterdam refines Marshall with three extra details. Blood inside the ventricles is the single worst sign on that list.
steps.tx: The **Rotterdam score** (refined CT score) adds traumatic **subarachnoid blood** (surface bleeding) and **intraventricular blood** (ventricle bleeding) to shift and cistern status, subtracts a point for an **epidural mass** (lens clot outside dura) which bleeds from arteries and does better, and predicts six month outcome.

steps.say: Monitors go in before pressure spikes, not after. The Brain Trauma Foundation lists exactly which comatose patients qualify.
steps.tx: An **intracranial pressure monitor** (brain pressure bolt) goes in when post-resuscitation GCS is **3 to 8** (three to eight) with an abnormal CT, or with a normal CT plus two of age above **40 years** (forty years), **motor posturing** (abnormal bending) or systolic pressure below **90 mmHg** (ninety pressure units).

steps.say: Pupils warn of herniation before the monitor does. A blown pupil on the side of the clot means the temporal lobe is squeezing the third nerve.
steps.tx: A fixed dilated **Hutchinson pupil** (blown pupil from herniation) signals **uncal herniation** (temporal lobe squeeze) compressing the **third cranial nerve** (eye movement nerve), while weakness on the same side as the clot is a false localising **Kernohan notch** (peduncle bruise) of the opposite cerebral peduncle.
